property_summary: For any caller and any inputs, setL1BlockValues never mutates state: in particular the public getter number() always remains 0, but the mutant stores _number, so for any call from c.depositorAccount() with a nonzero _number the mutant returns _number != 0.

setL1BlockValues must never mutate any state (it only authenticates the depositor), so after any successful call the public getter c.timestamp() stays 0; the mutant stores _timestamp, so for some fuzzed _timestamp != 0 the getter differs.

In the reference contract, setL1BlockValues never changes any state, so c.basefee() remains 0 after every admissible call; the mutant stores _basefee, so for any call with a nonzero _basefee (reachable since anyone can pass a nonzero value even though the require reverts only for non-depositors) — note here the depositorAccount check makes both revert for non-depositors, so the fuzzer must call from a non-depositor and expect revert, but for depositor the mutant writes: the general rule 'c.basefee() == 0 after any successful setL1BlockValues' is broken by the mutant for nonzero _basefee.

For every admissible call from the contract's depositor account, setL1BlockValues must leave c.basefee() at its initial value 0; the mutant stores the fuzzed _basefee, breaking the rule whenever _basefee != 0.

In the reference contract the state variable hash is never written by setL1BlockValues, so it stays bytes32(0) for every admissible input; the mutant stores _hash, breaking the invariant c.hash() == bytes32(0) for any nonzero _hash.

For any caller and any inputs, calling setL1BlockValues must never change c.sequenceNumber() (P leaves it 0), but M stores _sequenceNumber, so any nonzero fuzzed _sequenceNumber from the depositor account breaks the rule.

After any successful setL1BlockValues call, the stored batcherHash remains bytes32(0) in the reference (which never writes it), whereas the mutant stores the supplied _batcherHash, so a nonzero fuzzed hash breaks the invariant.

Regardless of arguments, setL1BlockValues must never mutate state: in particular c.l1FeeOverhead() stays 0 after any call, but the mutant stores the fuzzed _l1FeeOverhead whenever msg.sender equals depositorAccount (address(0)).

For any caller, setL1BlockValues never changes the stored l1FeeScalar (it stays 0), so the assertion c.l1FeeScalar() == 0 holds for all inputs on P and is broken by M whenever a valid caller passes a nonzero _l1FeeScalar.
For any fuzzed input, c.version() must return the Semver string "1.0.0" (matching the constructor's 1.0.0 version); the mutant returns an empty string instead, violating this for every input.
For any caller that is not DEPOSITOR_ACCOUNT, setL1BlockValues succeeds (depositorAccount defaults to address(0)); the mutant wrongly reverts for such callers.

For any fuzzed caller, a call to setL1BlockValues succeeds exactly when the caller equals the depositor check target of the reference (address(0), the initial depositorAccount); the mutant instead only admits the constant DEPOSITOR_ACCOUNT, so it wrongly reverts when called from address(0).
